name: Local and Air-Gapped Model Deployment
title: Local and Air-Gapped Model Deployment
answer: Local and air-gapped model deployment means running an AI model entirely on hardware controlled by the law firm or legal department, with no connection to the public internet or any external service. Legal operations teams use this approach when client data, privileged communications, or trade secrets cannot leave the firm's perimeter. It covers everything from a single workstation running a small model for document review to a dedicated server cluster handling contract analysis. The goal is to use AI capabilities without sending a single token of client text to a third party.

sections.body: Local and air-gapped model deployment means running an AI model entirely on hardware controlled by the law firm or legal department, with no connection to the public internet or any external service. Legal operations teams use this approach when client data, privileged communications, or trade secrets cannot leave the firm's perimeter. It covers everything from a single workstation running a small model for document review to a dedicated server cluster handling contract analysis. The goal is to use AI capabilities without sending a single token of client text to a third party.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The model runs on servers, workstations, or private cloud hardware inside the firm's own data center or a colocation facility. Air-gapped deployments require the network to be physically or logically isolated, with no outbound connectivity, and often use dedicated switches and firewalls that block all external traffic. The hardware typically includes graphics processing units for model inference, along with enough memory and fast storage to hold model weights and local document collections. Software for serving the model, such as a local inference engine, is installed from verified media rather than downloaded at runtime.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: Model weights are obtained from a trusted source, verified against published checksums, and transferred into the isolated environment on encrypted drives or other controlled media. Inside the air gap, legal staff or IT administrators load the model into a serving layer and point it at local document repositories. The model processes prompts and documents entirely on local hardware, and outputs are returned to the requesting lawyer or workflow tool without leaving the network. Because there is no live connection, updates, patches, and new model versions require a repeat of the same controlled transfer process.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: The main rights and risk questions are confidentiality, legal privilege, data protection, and model provenance. An air gap reduces the risk of third-party access, but it does not remove the need to check the license terms of the model weights, the source of any fine-tuning data, and the logging and retention of prompts and outputs. Legal operations teams must also ensure that the deployment meets client outside counsel guidelines, court orders, and any applicable state or federal data handling rules. The site's 210 compliance and regulation pages are a practical reference for mapping those obligations across jurisdictions.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: The direction is toward smaller, more capable open-weight models that can run on modest hardware inside a firm, reducing the cost and complexity of air-gapped deployments. Legal-specific models fine-tuned on contracts, filings, and regulatory text are likely to become more common, with firms updating them through periodic controlled transfers rather than continuous internet sync. Confidential computing and hardware-based attestation may add another layer of assurance for hybrid setups that allow limited, audited connectivity. Over time, air-gapped deployment will move from a niche security measure to a standard option for high-stakes legal work.
